newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian taxi drivers strike for tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: Serbian taxi drivers strike for tax cuts.

text.p: Taxi drivers in Serbia went on strike on Wednesday to demand tax cuts and cheaper imports of second hand cars.
"High taxes are making it impossible for us to earn a decent living," said a spokesman for Beotaxi, Belgrade's biggest taxi organisation.
Taxi drivers also want cuts in duty levied on imports of cars up to six years old to help them renew their fleet.
"As things stand now, we can only buy locally produced poor quality Zastavas or run-down but overpriced second hand cars on the local market," a Beotaxi driver told Reuters.
The latest strike has added to tension in Serbia, which has been shaken by a wave of worker protests as the economy worsens.
Serbia has an estimated 20,000 registered taxi drivers, of whom 10,000 are in Belgrade, which has a quarter of Yugoslavia's 11 million population.
"We are not answering calls as of six this morning, except for emergency cases", a Beotaxi telephone dispatcher said.
Serbian Minister for Private Enterprise Radoje Djukic said on Tuesday the strikers demands were justified.

"They froze their decision on a general strike a month ago pending agreement with the authorities. But the decision on taxes has not been reviewed despite the Serbian deputy finance minister's promises," Djukic told daily newspaper Politika Ekspres.
High unemployment and low wages have pushed many, even highly educated people, into cabbing.

"The authorities have allowed unlimited numbers of taxis on the streets because it means they can collect more taxes," a Beotaxi driver told Reuters. All cab drivers are subject to a lump tax, regardless of their turnover.
"We are prepared to spend the night in the streets until all our demands are met," Politika Ekspres quoted Milovoje Armus, head of the strike committee, as saying.
